title: Dutch build Fort Zeelandia
description: The Dutch East India Company settles at Tayouan and begins the fort that becomes the centre of its colony on Taiwan.

title: Spanish settle at Keelung
description: Spain founds a colony in northern Taiwan, which the Dutch take in 1642.

title: Koxinga takes Fort Zeelandia
description: After a nine-month siege the Dutch surrender to the Ming loyalist Koxinga, ending Dutch rule on Taiwan.

title: Battle of Penghu
description: The Qing admiral Shi Lang destroys the Tungning fleet, and the kingdom surrenders Taiwan to the Qing later that year.

title: Taiwan Prefecture established
description: The Qing court decides to keep Taiwan and makes it a prefecture of Fujian Province.

title: Lin Shuangwen rebellion
description: The largest uprising against Qing rule on Taiwan is put down after more than a year.

title: Japanese expedition to Taiwan
description: Japan sends troops to southern Taiwan after the killing of shipwrecked Ryukyuan sailors, its first overseas expedition of the Meiji era.

title: Taiwan becomes a province
description: The Qing separate Taiwan from Fujian as a province of its own, with Liu Mingchuan as its first governor.

title: Treaty of Shimonoseki
description: After losing the First Sino-Japanese War the Qing cede Taiwan and the Penghu Islands to Japan.

title: Republic of Formosa proclaimed
description: Officials and gentry on Taiwan declare a republic to resist the handover to Japan; it falls within five months.

title: Tapani incident
description: One of the largest armed uprisings against Japanese rule is suppressed.

title: Musha Incident
description: Seediq people attack Japanese residents at Musha, and the reprisals kill hundreds of Seediq.

title: Taiwan handed to the Republic of China
description: Japanese forces on Taiwan surrender to the Republic of China, which takes over the island's administration.

title: February 28 incident
description: Protests against the Nationalist administration spread across the island and are put down by troops, with thousands killed.

title: Republic of China government moves to Taipei
description: Having lost the civil war on the mainland, the Nationalist government relocates its capital to Taipei.

title: Second Taiwan Strait Crisis
description: The People's Republic of China begins shelling Kinmen, held by the Republic of China, opening weeks of fighting.

title: UN seat passes to the People's Republic
description: General Assembly Resolution 2758 gives China's seat at the United Nations to the People's Republic, and the Republic of China's delegates leave.

title: Kaohsiung Incident
description: Police break up a human rights rally and opposition leaders are jailed, which strengthens the democracy movement.

title: Martial law lifted
description: President Chiang Ching-kuo ends 38 years of martial law.

title: First direct presidential election
description: Voters elect the president directly for the first time and choose Lee Teng-hui.

title: Jiji earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake in central Taiwan kills more than 2,400 people.

title: First change of ruling party
description: Chen Shui-bian of the Democratic Progressive Party wins the presidency, ending more than fifty years of Kuomintang rule.

title: Sunflower Student Movement
description: Students occupy the legislature for more than three weeks in protest at a trade agreement with the People's Republic of China.
